messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] winhr
messages.body_plain:
Hi Tad,
Winhr currently only works with one parameter setting. You will have to process your data twice with part2 to get the results for two settings I am afraid.
I have a part5 under development which does facilitate multiple winhr settings and hope to be able to add this to the functionality later this year.
Vincent

>

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Error in array - data must be of a vector type
messages.subject_clean: [GGIR] Error in array - data must be of a vector type
messages.body_plain:
It sounds like that the data folder is not recognized or the data itself is not recognized.

1. If working in RStudio under linux don't use ~ as reference to your root, but use the exact path, e.g. /home/username/myfolder instead of ~/myfolder

2. Another common mistake is to not specify the correct path for your data (argument datadir). To verify this: set argument print.filename=TRUE, this will print the filename in the consule before it tries to load it in g.part1. This will help you to check that the code is trying to load the correct file.

3. Finally, in some computing environments it is worth checking that you as a user have file access permissions.

Vincent

messages.subject: response to question Jonathan regarding export of calibrated raw data
messages.subject_clean: response to question Jonathan regarding export of calibrated raw data
messages.body_plain:
Message:
Hi Vincent, Thank you for providing this group. I am doing some secondary analysis of ActiGraph data. The data are .csv in the appropriate format, but it does not have timestamps. I am new to R. Do you have suggestions on how I can calibrate and filter 3 columns of data and output it to a new csv file? From this I already have SAS code to apply the timestamps. Thank you!

Response:
The quickest solution would be to use GGIR function g.calibrate in R for deriving the calibration coefficients and then use these coefficients as input to your SAS code.

GGIR is currently not able to export calibrated raw data. I would like to implement something like that, but have limited time at the moment.

regards,
Vincent

messages.subject: Error in g.part1
messages.body_plain:
Hi Vincent et all,

I've just arrived to your package  and I'm trying to process a two day .bin file from a GeneActiv device.
While executing g.part1 while "getting meta data" this error occurs:
    Error in butter.default(n = 5, Wc, type = c("pass")) :
    butter: critical frequencies must be in (0 1)

Before trying with g.part1 I've done without problems the "long way":
I=(g.inspectfile(datafile) -> C=g.calibrate(datafile) -> M=g.getmeta(datafile) -> g.impute(M, I) -> g.analyse(I, C, M, IMP) -> g.plot(IMP, M, I, durplot = 4)

Do you have any idea of the reason of it?
Thanks in advance

Iñigo Zunzunegui

messages.subject_clean: Error in array - data must be of a vector type
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jonathan,
I've just solved the same error.
In my case the problem was produced because in a couple of fields (i.e. Exercise Type: & Subject Notes:) there where some odd characters (i.e. accents or spanich letter "ñ") that made null appear in the .bin file (you can edit the .bin with an editor to check this point).
In a little file some warnings appeared advising that in certain lines seemed to be a nul but in  a bigger file the error was shown.

Iñigo
